questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

It is believed that physical exercise is ______ for creating a balance between the body and the mind.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Essential.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ** **The word **"essential"** means something **necessary** or **required**.

 
 
• **Example-** *Vitamin is an essential element to strengthen human immunity*.
 
• Therefore, the complete sentence will be: **"It is believed that physical exercise is essential for creating a balance between the body and the mind."**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The word "**forceful**" stands for **being powerful or strong**.

 
 
• **Example-** *He bears a forceful willpower.*
 
 
 
• **"Demanding"** refers to something **which is very much wanted.**
 
• **Example**- *Last year, the club was demanding a lot of money from the investors to organise the annual fest.*
 
• **"Increased"** stands for something which **has grown** over time.
 
 
• **Example**: *The production of paddy has increased quite a lot this year*.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Flowing**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Flowed"** refers to **past tense.**
 
• **"Flow"** can be used in the present tense only when** the subject will be first person or second person or third person plural number.**
 
• **"Flows"** cannot be used as **it is a finite verb**, and according to English grammar, **a simple sentence cannot carry more than one finite verb.**
 
• This is also the reason that "flowed" or "flow" cannot be used as they are also finite verbs.
 
• **"Flowing"** is the correct form that is suitable here as it functions as a **gerund** here.
 
• Therefore the complete sentence is, "**It is made by Sharavati river flowing through the Western Ghats**." ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When **the participle form of the verb** is used as a noun it is called** gerund**.

 
 
• **​Example**- *He loves swimming in the river.*Here swimming is a gerund.
 
 
 
• **A finite verb** refers to a verb **that is governed by the person and number of the subject.**

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **the**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The complete sentence will be, "... **during monsoons *the* river is swollen with water.**"
 
• "**The**" is a **definite article** used to **refer to a particular thing**.
 
• The phrase "**The river**", **refers to the particular Sharavati river**.
 
• It helps people to understand about **which particular object we are talking**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Both "**a**" and "**an**" are **indefinite article** as it does not **refer to any particular thing**.
 
• If we use "**a" river** instead of "the river", it can** refer to any river**.
 
• Using "**the**" before the river helps us to understand **which particular river it is referring to**.
